title: common: offer a passphrase for every encrypted SSH key format
message:
common: offer a passphrase for every encrypted SSH key format

The repository dialog greys out its passphrase field for a key that needs
no passphrase. It decided that by looking for the word ENCRYPTED on the
first line of the key file. Only a PKCS#8 key says so there. A classic
PEM key says it on the second line, and an OpenSSH key does not say it at
all.

The check now reads all three formats, and the dialog offers the field
whenever the key really is encrypted.

title: Handle orphaned GL objects and contexts
message:
Handle orphaned GL objects and contexts

The 3d canvas creates its own unshared context.  Since GL object names
are per-share group, using `glDeleteBuffers` while in the wrong context
(footprint 3d preview) would destroy unrelated content.  We were using
`wxGLCanvas::SetCurrent()` but this doesn't work after GdkWindow is
gone.  So we need to introduce a concept of orphaed objects that are
going to be deleted but right now, we still need the references

title: Verify the GL context is current before issuing GL commands
message:
Verify the GL context is current before issuing GL commands

Every 2D canvas shares one context group, and a canvas whose window is
already destroyed cannot be made current.  Teardown then deleted a
sibling's framebuffer, which is not a shared object, leaving that canvas
presenting its last frame.

title: pcbnew: fix skew errors that come and go on an unchanged board
message:
pcbnew: fix skew errors that come and go on an unchanged board

DRC joins a net's tracks into runs before measuring it. It found the end of
a run by counting the track ends that met at a point, and it counted ends
on every layer. So a via looked like a branch. Which tracks got joined then
depended on the order they sat in memory, and editing the board changes
that. A short piece of track beside a via was sometimes counted twice, and
a tuned differential pair failed the skew rule on one run and passed on the
next.

The count now ignores other layers and reads the board as it was loaded. A
net measures the same every time.

(cherry picked from commit 22ad54e8c0f017611ca1b2caa83d426567e7baac)

title: Fall back to software before a fatal GPU OOM
message:
Fall back to software before a fatal GPU OOM

On large boards the GL canvas can request more video memory than the
GPU has, tripping a driver-level abort (e.g. NVIDIA "Error code: 6")
that kills the process before glGetError() can report it, so the
existing OpenGL to Cairo recovery never gets a chance to run.

To fix this, we attempt to avoid the extra allocation.  This commit
tries multiple ways to ensure we don't hit our card ceiling.  Instead of
allocating double memory while holding the original data, if that would
overflow, we either hold the temp memory in RAM or fallback to software.
We avoid this for drivers that don't respond to the VRAM query

(cherry picked from commit ca140e2c8524e47c0944ed8701ae1ac351fad898)
